name: DOMINO
evaluates: manipulation of moving objects (interception and tracking) under three levels of motion complexity, scored by success rate and a continuous manipulation score
improves: earlier simulation benchmarks assume a static world in which only the robot changes the state, and dynamic manipulation data for training VLAs was scarce
setup: SAPIEN; built on RoboTwin 2.0; five embodiments (Aloha-AgileX, Franka Panda, Piper, UR5-WSG, ARX-X5), main experiments on Aloha-AgileX
scale: 35 tasks; 110K+ expert trajectories; 3 dynamics levels (constant velocity, polynomial, multi-segment with abrupt transitions); speed coefficient alpha
real_validation: ACT, RDT-1B, pi0.5 and PUMA were fine-tuned with 50 teleoperated demos per task and tested on 5 DOMINO tasks (20 trials each) on an AgileX Piper (averages 7%, 8%, 24%, 42%); method transfer only, no sim-real correlation reported.
vla_results: ACT, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, RDT-1B, pi0, pi0.5, InternVLA-M1, PUMA; static-trained policies drop below 8% success on dynamic tasks, dynamic fine-tuning adds under 3 points, PUMA reaches 17.2% SR
status: Code, dataset and PUMA weights released; no leaderboard; extended by DOMINO-Long (D2-VLA), used in the DSDyn-VLA appendix, cited as prior work by MotionForge; PUMA is a baseline in ReflexBench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment and project page. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. The paper's stated 6.3-point gain over baselines could not be reconciled with the extracted table.

name: DOM (Dynamic Object Manipulation benchmark, DynamicVLA)
evaluates: manipulation of objects in motion along nine sub-dimensions of interaction, perception and generalization, including closed-loop reactivity and disturbance robustness
improves: robot datasets are mostly static and teleoperation cannot track fast objects; inference latency makes actions stale by execution time
setup: Isaac Sim with an automatic demonstrator driven by object pose and velocity; 3D-FRONT scenes and Objaverse objects; Franka Emika Panda and AgileX PiPER
scale: 200K synthetic episodes; 2.8K scenes; 206 objects; 2K real episodes; 3 dimensions x 3 sub-dimensions
real_validation: The benchmark has its own real-robot arm: 16 real tasks on Franka and PiPER, 60 trials per task (960 trials per method); no sim-real correlation statistic is reported.
vla_results: Diffusion Policy, ACT, OpenVLA-OFT, pi0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T-N1.5, RTC, VLA-Adapter-Pro, VLASH, DynamicVLA; DynamicVLA 47.06% average success vs 12.33% for the best baseline (VLASH)
status: Project page available; DynamicVLA is a baseline in ReflexBench and DynBench, and DOM is cited as prior work by MotionForge; no leaderboard found
note: Venue is the arXiv comment field ('NeurIPS 2026'); not checked against the NeurIPS site. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: DOMINO-Long
evaluates: retaining cues seen early in an episode (object locations, presentation order, colour instructions) while manipulating moving objects over several stages
improves: original DOMINO tasks are short-horizon and place weak demands on long-term memory
setup: RoboTwin 2.0 / DOMINO; Aloha-AgileX bimanual robot
scale: 10 multi-stage tasks; 50 demonstrations per task (500 total, 227,208 records); episodes of 201-911 steps
real_validation: The proposed D2-VLA was compared with pi0.5 and MemoryVLA on eight long-horizon tasks (four static, four dynamic) on a Unitree G1D; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: PUMA 20.6%, pi0.5 35.4%, D2-VLA 60.0% success
status: Introduced inside a method paper (D2-VLA); code repository and project page listed; no independent adoption seen
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. Physics engine not stated in the extracted text; inherited from DOMINO.

name: MotionForge
evaluates: long-horizon manipulation of moving objects under factorized domain shifts (object, background, lighting, motion speed) with latency-aware real-time execution
improves: existing dynamic benchmarks do not jointly cover diverse motion patterns, long horizons, systematic domain shift and latency-aware evaluation
setup: Isaac Sim; positions itself against DOM, DOMINO and PhysMani-Bench; robot embodiment not stated in the extracted text
scale: 40 tasks in 4 scene families (17 long-horizon); 11 motion patterns; about 20,000 demonstration episodes; 4 shift axes plus joint shift
vla_results: Diffusion Policy, ACT, SmolVLA, X-VLA, pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, FastWAM; best in-domain result is ACT at 22.2%, best under joint shift 5.85%; freezing the scene adds 21.7-27.5 points
status: New preprint; no code or project URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: ReflexBench
evaluates: reaction-critical manipulation where inference latency separates perception from execution: conveyor pick-and-place, ball catching, interception, throwing, rotating-peg insertion
improves: existing dynamic benchmarks evaluate only and do not provide a common framework for studying anticipation together with inference efficiency
setup: Simulation with a real-time-factor metric; simulator and simulated robot not stated in the extracted text; real robot is an AgileX Piper
scale: 6 tasks; 200 demonstrations per task
real_validation: Three tasks (conveyor pick-and-place, button pressing, ball catching) were run on an AgileX Piper with ReflexVLA, PUMA and SmolVLA, 20 runs per task; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: ReflexVLA 50.4%, PUMA 50.2%, SmolVLA 38.3%, DynamicVLA 37.3%, pi0.5 36.9%, OpenVLA-OFT 36.0%, VLA-Adapter 30.3%
status: Introduced inside a method paper (Reflex); project page listed; no independent adoption seen
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. Simulator name could not be confirmed.

name: DynBench
evaluates: vision-based manipulation of moving objects: conveyor picking and sorting, dropping and stacking onto moving targets, insertion into a moving hole, grasping rolling objects
improves: the state-based Kinetix benchmark does not exercise the visual pipeline of a VLA in dynamic scenes
setup: MuJoCo; Franka Panda; four real dynamic tasks ported to simulation and expanded
scale: 9 tasks; 100 rule-generated demonstrations per task
real_validation: Four tasks (conveyor picking, dynamic dropping, dynamic stacking, mobile pouring) were run on an AgileX Piper, 50 trials each; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: pi0.5 9.7%, RTC 19.4%, VLASH 27.1%, DynamicVLA 34.3%, DSDyn-VLA 48.4% average success
status: Introduced inside a method paper (DSDyn-VLA); code promised but no URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: PhysMani-Bench
evaluates: manipulation of fast-moving targets (moving belts, rotating racks) at normal and high speed in 3D scenes
improves: benchmarks focus on static or quasi-static manipulation and dynamic-target manipulation is little studied
setup: Extended from RLBench; Franka Emika Panda in simulation; Astribot S1 for real tests
scale: 16 tasks (8 groups x 2 speeds); 160 trajectories per task (2,560 total)
real_validation: Four dynamic tasks on an Astribot S1 (64 trials per task) compared PhysMani with a baseline; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: PhysMani 45.9%, 3DFA 37.8%, 3DDA 35.1%, Act3D 27.1%, ManiGaussian 22.5%, pi0.5 8.3% mean success
status: Introduced inside a method paper; code and data repository listed; cited by MotionForge
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Mostly 3D policies; pi0.5 is the only VLA baseline. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-Plus
evaluates: robustness of LIBERO-trained VLAs to seven controlled perturbation types: object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language instruction, lighting, background texture, sensor noise
improves: near-ceiling LIBERO scores hide brittleness; earlier robustness tests used few scenarios and gave no fine-grained analysis within a perturbation dimension
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo); Franka Panda
scale: 10,030 perturbed test tasks; 7 dimensions with 21 sub-dimensions; 5 difficulty levels; 20K+ training trajectories released
vla_results: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT (three variants), pi0, pi0-FAST, NORA, WorldVLA, UniVLA, RIPT-VLA; success falls from about 95% to below 30%; camera and initial-state shifts hurt most, language changes least
status: Widely reused (LIBERO-MAX, LIBERO-Safety, IndustrialVLA-Bench, RoboTwin 2.0-Plus study); results table maintained in the GitHub README
note: arXiv title is 'In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models'; the CVPR 2026 poster page lists it as 'A Progressive Robustness Benchmark for Visual-Language-Action Models'. The CVF open-access page returned 403.

name: LIBERO-PRO
evaluates: whether LIBERO success reflects memorization, by perturbing object attributes, initial positions, task instructions and environments, alone and in combination
improves: the standard LIBERO train and test configuration lets overfitted models score near-perfectly while collapsing under small changes
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo)
scale: 4 perturbation dimensions applied to the LIBERO suites; task count not extracted
vla_results: OpenVLA, pi0, pi0.5; over 90% on standard LIBERO falls to 0.0% under the generalized setting; pi0.5 retains 0.38 on position changes
status: Code released; reused by LIBERO-MAX (2,400 cases) and cited by most later LIBERO variants
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. No venue on the arXiv record.

name: LIBERO-X
evaluates: robustness under coupled, multi-factor shifts graded in five levels: local spatial, extended spatial, scene topology, visual attributes, semantically equivalent instructions
improves: existing benchmarks test isolated shifts, and LIBERO test sets closely mirror low-diversity training data
setup: MuJoCo; LIBERO-style environments; single arm with gripper
scale: 600 tasks in 100 scenes; 2,520 VR-teleoperated demonstrations; 5 perturbation levels; 4 multi-label task attributes
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT, pi0, X-VLA, GR00T-N1.5, pi0.5; pi0.5 falls from 65.2% (level 1) to 18.0% (level 5); three-step tasks near zero
status: Project page available; no leaderboard or code URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-VPro
evaluates: closed-loop visual robustness when the visual evidence itself is corrupted during execution: degradation, camera staleness, cross-view inconsistency, task-relevant scene variation
improves: earlier suites perturb scene or task configuration while the observation stream stays temporally coherent and internally consistent
setup: LIBERO (40 tasks from four suites); real checks on Franka Research 3
scale: 40 tasks; 4 dimensions, 12 challenge categories, 96 settings, 3,296 task-condition cases; about 196,000 simulated episodes
real_validation: pi0.5 and LaWAM were run on a Franka Research 3 under four of the conditions (10 trials per condition, 200 rollouts); trends were reported as broadly consistent with simulation, without a correlation coefficient.
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT, pi0, pi0.5 and three world-action models (FastWAM, LingBot-VA, LaWAM); nominal 92-99% falls to 56-67% on average; view loss and stale cameras are most disruptive
status: Project page available; new preprint
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-Occ
evaluates: robustness to scene-induced occlusion of the manipulated object, the receptacle, or both, at three severity levels
improves: VLA benchmarks implicitly assume task-relevant objects are fully visible in the input observation
setup: LIBERO (four suites); Franka arm
scale: 2,000 occluded task instances (500 per suite); 3 occlusion types x 3 severities
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT 95.75% to 47.95%, pi0.5 90.00% to 40.55%, UniVLA 88.25% to 57.10%; the proposed VIM reaches 65.05%
status: Code repository listed; benchmark-plus-method paper
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. The extraction named PyBullet as the engine, which conflicts with other LIBERO-derived papers (robosuite / MuJoCo); engine left unconfirmed.

name: LIBERO-MAX
evaluates: task completion when the world changes after the policy has begun acting: target or receptacle relocation, camera shift, lighting switch, noise onset, distractors, obstacle insertion
improves: existing benchmarks set external conditions at reset, so mid-episode change is untested
setup: LIBERO; cases drawn from LIBERO-Plus (5,600) and LIBERO-PRO (2,400)
scale: 8,000 Base/Dynamic pairs (16,000 rollouts per policy); 8 event types with 1,000 pairs each
vla_results: 14 policies including pi0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, X-VLA, Xiaomi-Robotics-0, MolmoAct2, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.7, VLA-JEPA and five WAMs; every policy loses 11.0-25.7 points; WAMs are not consistently better or worse than VLAs
status: Project page available; new preprint
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-RECOVER
evaluates: failure recovery in four difficulty levels: action retry, action adaptation, object-state recovery, environmental recovery
improves: benchmarks evaluate completion from predefined initial states and do not assess failure recognition, state recovery or replanning
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo); Franka
scale: 130 subtasks across 4 suites; 2,178 recovery scenarios; 4 recovery levels; 10 trials per scenario
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT, GR00T-N1.5, pi0, pi0-FAST, Wan2-Policy, Cosmos-Predict2-Policy; all lose more than half of their performance after failures; recovery success about 40% at level 1 and about 3% at level 4
status: Release announced, no URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-CTRL
evaluates: compound robustness: whether outcomes under simultaneous perturbations can be predicted from outcomes under each single perturbation on the same matched instance
improves: LIBERO-Plus tested selected pairwise combinations but did not link constituent and compound outcomes per evaluation instance
setup: LIBERO (four suites)
scale: 40 tasks; 6 axes (camera, lighting, robot pose, sensor, actuation, language); 3 severity levels; 400 matched configurations; 10,400 rollouts per checkpoint
vla_results: pi0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, SmolVLA, VLA-JEPA, PredVLA, MINERVA; up to 29.0% of configurations change outcome between single-axis conjunction and the simultaneous condition while the aggregate barely moves
status: Code and per-rollout outcomes in a public repository; new preprint
note: Paper title is 'Beyond Single-Axis Testing: Paired Evaluation of Compound Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Policies'. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus
evaluates: robustness of bimanual policies, comparing world-action models with VLAs, under noise, lighting, camera, robot initial state, background, layout and language perturbations
improves: the LIBERO-Plus perturbation protocol existed only for single-arm LIBERO, and WAM-versus-VLA robustness had not been compared
setup: RoboTwin 2.0; Aloha-AgileX dual arm; paired with LIBERO-Plus for single-arm results
scale: 7 perturbation types; task count not extracted
vla_results: LingBot-VA 74.2%, Fast-WAM 72.7%, MOTUS 71.5%, pi0.5 58.6%, X-VLA 53.1% overall; WAMs hold up under visual perturbations but struggle with camera and robot-state changes
status: Evaluation code page listed; introduced inside a study paper
note: Paper title is 'Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study'. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: Eva-VLA
evaluates: worst-case robustness to physically plausible variations found by black-box optimization: 3D object transformations, illumination changes, adversarial patches
improves: adversarial-patch studies violate physical plausibility or need gradient access and do not cover the range of real physical variation
setup: LIBERO (four suites); real checks on an AgileX Piper
scale: 40 tasks; 3 variation families with 9 continuous parameters; 500 rollouts per suite
real_validation: Three 'put A into B' tasks, one per variation type, were run on an AgileX Piper and failures were reported as consistent with simulation; no correlation statistic.
vla_results: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, pi0.5; failure rates rise to 68-88% under 3D transformations; OpenVLA exceeds 90% failure on LIBERO-Long
status: No code or project URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: VLATest
evaluates: generation-based fuzz testing of VLAs over target and confounding objects, lighting, camera pose, unseen objects and instruction mutations
improves: VLA evaluation relied on small hand-made scene sets, with no automated testing framework
setup: ManiSkill2 with visual-matching rendering; tasks follow Open X-Embodiment-trained model setups; robot not specified in the extracted text
scale: 4 tasks; 18,604 generated scenes; 10 testing operators
vla_results: RT-1 (three checkpoints), RT-1-X, Octo-small, Octo-base, OpenVLA-7b; average success 12.4%, 6.0%, 1.2% and 0.5% on the four tasks; only 34% of passing cases survive camera mutations
status: Code and the 18,604 generated scenes released; LADEV evaluates the same seven models
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LADEV
evaluates: automated robustness testing in which scenes are generated from natural-language descriptions and instructions are paraphrased
improves: there was no platform for automatically testing and evaluating VLA models
setup: SAPIEN / ManiSkill2; extends SimplerEnv
scale: 4 tasks; 4,000+ generated scenes; multiple paraphrased instructions per scene
vla_results: RT-1 (three checkpoints), RT-1-X, Octo-small, Octo-base, OpenVLA-7b; success drops 10-30% on unseen objects and 5-15% under paraphrase; put-on and put-in tasks near zero
status: Project site available; code release was pending in the paper
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: PVEP (Manipulation Facing Threats)
evaluates: physical visual threats to VLAs: blur, noise, brightness, typographic visual prompts, and adversarial patches from black-box to white-box
improves: no earlier work had evaluated open-source VLA models against physical security threats
setup: VIMA simulator and SimplerEnv
scale: 20 tasks (14 VIMA, 6 SimplerEnv); 4 threat categories
vla_results: LLaRA and OpenVLA; blur raises failure by about 47 points for both; white-box patches reach 94.5% (LLaRA) and 100% (OpenVLA) failure
status: Project page available
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: AttackVLA
evaluates: a common protocol for adversarial and backdoor attacks on VLAs, measuring effectiveness, transferability and targeted long-horizon misbehaviour
improves: attacks were evaluated on different models and setups with no unified framework
setup: LIBERO (four suites); real tests on a 7-DoF Franka
scale: 40 tasks; 6 adversarial and 3 backdoor attacks
real_validation: TMA, TabVLA and BackdoorVLA were run against pi0-FAST on a Franka arm (attack success 42.5%, 20% and 50%); replication of attacks, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, pi0-FAST; targeted backdoor success 75.35%, 51.63% and 48.23%; pi0-FAST is the most robust to adversarial attacks
status: No code or project URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: RoboStress
evaluates: robustness to robot execution errors from mechanics: Stribeck friction, gear backlash, joint compliance, gravity-compensation error
improves: robustness studies inject synthetic action noise and leave execution errors from the robot itself unexplored
setup: MuJoCo 3.7.0 with robosuite 1.4.1; LIBERO (four suites); real tests on AgileX Piper arms
scale: 40 tasks; 4 error types combined into 7 deployment scenarios
real_validation: A self-compensating VLA was tested on two AgileX Piper arms with different wear on four tasks (76% vs 43% for the base policy on one arm); method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: pi0 and pi0.5 with domain-randomization and RobustVLA baselines; base pi0.5 49.1% and pi0 41.7% under stress; self-compensation raises them to 56.6% and 44.2%
status: Code release announced, no URL found
note: Paper title is 'Taming VLAs under Robot Execution Errors: Self-Compensation and Stress Testing'. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: RoboTwin-Phys
evaluates: sensitivity to physical-parameter variation: mass, centre of mass, friction, restitution, joint damping, table tilt and height, external force
improves: benchmarks randomize appearance and layout but keep physical parameters at nominal values
setup: RoboTwin 2.0; bimanual
scale: 50 tasks; 13 physical dimensions; 5,000+ expert episodes annotated with physical parameters
vla_results: Fast-WAM 91.88% to 44.24%, Motus 88.66% to 39.60%, FACT 88.40% to 39.14%, Galaxea G0.5 93.70% to 37.82%, pi0.5 82.74% to 31.60% (clean vs physical randomization)
status: Technical report; no code URL found
note: arXiv comment describes it as a 'technical report for a benchmark'. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: NEBULA
evaluates: per-capability diagnosis (control, perception, language, dynamic adaptation, spatial reasoning, robustness) plus stress tests of inference frequency, latency, stability and adaptability
improves: a single end-task success metric gives no skill diagnosis and no measure of robustness to perturbation; data formats are fragmented
setup: SAPIEN / ManiSkill3; single-arm tasks; unified data from ManiSkill, LeRobot and BEHAVIOR-1K formats
scale: 6 capability families at 3 difficulty levels; 4 stress tests at 3 pressure levels; about 216,000 trajectories
vla_results: GR00T-N1.5, SpatialVLA, RDT-1B, MT-ACT, Diffusion Policy, ACT; perception and language are strong, spatial reasoning is weak, dynamic adaptation and robustness scores are near zero
status: Project page available; no leaderboard or code URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. Task count was not clearly stated in the extracted text.

name: VLA-Arena
evaluates: structured difficulty along task structure, language and vision, covering safety constraints, distractors, extrapolation to unseen objects and compositions, and long horizons
improves: earlier benchmarks are static task collections that do not integrate robustness with extrapolation and overlook safety
setup: MuJoCo; LIBERO-style BDDL task definitions; Franka
scale: 170 tasks in 11 suites under 4 dimensions (Safety, Distractor, Extrapolation, Long Horizon); levels L0-L2; language W0-W4 and vision V0-V4; datasets with 10, 30 or 50 trajectories per task
real_validation: Policies were run on a Franka Research 3 on tasks from all four dimensions; degradation with difficulty and failure modes matched simulation qualitatively, with no correlation coefficient.
vla_results: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, pi0, pi0-FAST, UniVLA, SmolVLA; steep degradation from L0 to L2; high success is often reached by violating safety constraints
status: Open-source framework with leaderboard on the project site; reused by BeSafe-Bench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: RoboView-Bias
evaluates: visual bias in grasping agents: how success varies with object colour, camera orientation and pose, distance, shape and initial position
improves: benchmarks emphasize generalization and perturbation robustness, with little systematic quantification of visual bias
setup: RoboVerse with MuJoCo backend; single arm; grasping only
scale: 2,127 task instances; factors include 141 colours, 9 camera orientations, 21 camera poses, 9 distance scales
vla_results: VLM-driven agents MOKA and SimpleAgent (GPT-4o, Qwen-VL-Max) and pi0; pi0 46.53% average success with 53.05% coefficient of variation across factors
status: No code or project URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. Only one VLA (pi0) is evaluated.

name: GemBench
evaluates: generalization of vision-language manipulation policies in four levels: new placements, new rigid objects, new articulated objects, unseen long-horizon tasks
improves: RLBench-style evaluation tests seen tasks; VIMA-Bench has simple skills and Colosseum targets environment perturbations rather than new tasks
setup: RLBench (CoppeliaSim); real tests on a UR5
scale: 16 training tasks (31 variations, 3,100 demonstrations); 44 test tasks (92 variations) in 4 levels; 7 action primitives
real_validation: 3D-LOTUS and 3D-LOTUS++ were trained on 20 demos per variation for 7 real variations on a UR5 and tested on 7 seen and 7 unseen variations; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: Hiveformer, PolarNet, RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, 3D-LOTUS, 3D-LOTUS++ (no VLA in the original paper); level 1 up to 94.3%, level 4 at most 0.3% except 3D-LOTUS++ at 17.4%
status: Code and dataset public; project page maintained by the authors; 3D-LOTUS++ from this paper is a baseline in AGNOSTOS and ArtiBench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. The extraction called RLBench 'PyBullet-based', which conflicts with other RLBench papers (CoppeliaSim).

name: AGNOSTOS
evaluates: zero-shot cross-task generalization to unseen tasks in two levels: partial semantic overlap with training tasks, and entirely novel scenarios
improves: existing benchmarks assess within-task generalization and leave zero-shot cross-task generalization unexplored
setup: RLBench; real tests on an xArm7 with DH-Robotics gripper
scale: 18 seen RLBench tasks (3,600 demonstrations); 23 unseen tasks (13 level-1, 10 level-2)
real_validation: The proposed X-ICM was tested zero-shot on five real tasks on an xArm7 (20 executions per task) using demos from other tasks; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: PerAct, RVT, RVT-2, Sigma-Agent, Instant Policy, R3M, D4R, OpenVLA, RDT, pi0, LLARVA, SAM2Act, 3D-LOTUS++, VoxPoser, X-ICM; pi0 17.5% on unseen tasks, X-ICM (72B) 30.1%
status: Project page and code available; no venue on the arXiv record
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. The extracted margins over pi0 were not mutually consistent, so only the absolute numbers are given.

name: HiMan-Bench (RoboHiMan)
evaluates: compositional generalization in long-horizon manipulation under perturbation, separating planning failure from execution failure via vanilla, decoupled and coupled evaluation modes
improves: existing benchmarks cannot tell whether failures come from planning, execution or sensitivity to environmental perturbation
setup: CoppeliaSim / PyRep; extends DeCoBench tasks with Colosseum perturbation factors; Franka Panda
scale: 258 tasks (114 atomic and 144 compositional, including perturbed versions); 12 perturbation factors; 4 progressive training-data levels
real_validation: pi0.5 was run on a Mobile ALOHA arm on 4 atomic and 4 compositional tasks with distractor, position and human-intervention perturbations (vanilla 17.5% to 10%, with rule-based planner 47.5% to 27.5%); qualitative replication only.
vla_results: RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, pi0, pi0.5; near-zero on compositional tasks without a planner; with a rule-based planner RVT-2 reaches 39.5%; VLM planners lag rule-based ones
status: Project page available; listed as under review
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: DeCoBench
evaluates: zero-shot composition of learned atomic skills into unseen long-horizon 3D manipulation sequences
improves: multi-task imitation policies trained on atomic tasks fail on longer compositions, and no benchmark isolated this
setup: RLBench; Franka Emika Panda
scale: 10 atomic tasks (50 demonstrations each); 12 compositional long-horizon tasks
real_validation: DeCo-augmented policies were trained on 6 real atomic tasks and tested on 9 novel long-horizon tasks (53.33% vs 0% without DeCo); method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, ARP (3D policies, no VLA); baselines are near 0% on compositional tasks; with DeCo 66.67%, 21.53% and 58.06%
status: Project page available; extended by HiMan-Bench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment ('RAL 2026'). Introduced inside the DeCo method paper. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: ClevrSkills
evaluates: compositional generalization: whether models trained on simple motor skills can compose them for intermediate and complex tasks, including low-level execution
improves: VIMA-style benchmarks test high-level planning and not closed-loop plan-and-execute with low-level control
setup: ManiSkill2; UFACTORY xArm 6 with vacuum gripper (Franka Panda also available)
scale: 33 tasks in 3 levels (12 simple, 15 intermediate, 6 complex); about 330K trajectories
vla_results: JAT, RoboFlamingo, Octo, StreamRoboLM; level-0 success 24-63%; level 1 and level 2 stay at or below about 6% even after fine-tuning
status: Code and dataset released by Qualcomm AI Research
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: INT-ACT
evaluates: generalization boundaries of VLAs along object diversity, language complexity and vision-language reasoning, separating correct intention from successful execution
improves: SimplerEnv has few tasks, and imitation-learning benchmarks lack language variation
setup: ManiSkill2 / SimplerEnv (expanded from 4 to 50 BridgeV2 tasks); WidowX
scale: 50 tasks; 3 categories with 10 sub-categories
vla_results: pi0 (fine-tuned, from scratch, with rephrasing), SpatialVLA, Magma, Octo; intention is correct in 80-100% of cases while task success drops sharply on out-of-distribution variants
status: Project page and code available; arXiv comment says under review
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-OOD
evaluates: out-of-distribution recombination of skills seen in training: tasks that require stitching sub-trajectories never shown together
improves: there was no benchmark of tasks that VLAs could plausibly complete but currently cannot; standard LIBERO is near ceiling
setup: LIBERO; derived from the goal, object and spatial suites

improves: benchmarks test physical reasoning separately from execution, or measure policies without requiring reasoning
setup: robosuite (MuJoCo); single-arm and bimanual Franka with parallel-jaw and suction grippers
scale: 35 tasks in 7 categories; about 14K trajectories
vla_results: Diffusion Policy 0.24, pi0.5 0.15 and GR00T N1.5 0.02 mean success after fine-tuning (zero-shot at most 0.02); a GPT-based agent reaches 11.3% with vision
status: Project site available; full data and code release pending

name: SafeVLA-Bench
evaluates: the gap between success and safe success: excessive contact, disturbing bystander objects, destabilizing held objects and self-contact, checked post hoc with temporal-logic specifications
improves: VLA benchmarks record binary completion and miss safety-relevant behaviour along the trajectory
setup: MuJoCo; wraps LIBERO and RoboCasa-365; Franka and Panda-with-Omron setups
scale: 58 tasks (40 LIBERO, 18 RoboCasa-365 families); 8 constraint families; about 18,000 episodes; metrics include success-but-unsafe rate and violation severity index
real_validation: A pilot on an SO-101 arm with video-labelled checks of two constraint families found 4 unsafe successes among 26 successful rollouts; pilot only, no correlation.
vla_results: 18 policies on LIBERO and 9 on RoboCasa-365, including OpenVLA, pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.6/N1.7, X-VLA, SmolVLA, Cosmos-Policy; policies above 90% success still have 18-28% unsafe episodes; 38-56% of RoboCasa-365 successes violate a constraint
status: Project site available; code and data release announced
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: LIBERO-Safety
evaluates: physical and semantic safety: affordance-aware grasping, human-robot interaction, tabletop avoidance, free-space hand and object avoidance, semantic safety reasoning
improves: safety methods are tested under inconsistent protocols in static scenes with simple tabletop obstacles
setup: Extends LIBERO-Plus; Panda arm; collision-free demonstrations from a CuRobo keypose pipeline
scale: 75 tasks (5 suites x 5 tasks x 3 levels); 19,664 collision-free demonstrations
vla_results: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, pi0, pi0.5, UniVLA, VLA-JEPA, GR00T N1.5 and N1.6, plus RoboBrain2.0 and RynnBrain-CoP for refusal; pi0.5 is best at 35-88% across suites
status: Project page available
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: SafeLIBERO
evaluates: collision avoidance while completing LIBERO tasks, with obstacles placed near the target or across the motion path
improves: objects rarely collide with the arm in the original LIBERO, so it contains no safety-critical scenarios
setup: robosuite; LIBERO; Franka Emika Panda
scale: 16 tasks; 32 scenarios (2 obstacle levels per task); 1,600 episodes
real_validation: Two tasks at two safety levels were run on a Franka Panda with pi0.5-DROID and the proposed safety layer; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: pi0.5 18.7% collision avoidance and 50.9% success; OpenVLA-OFT 15.1% and 22.8%; AEGIS 77.9% and 68.1%
status: Introduced inside the VLSA / AEGIS method paper; code and project page public
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: Safety-CHORES
evaluates: safety constraints in mobile manipulation: corners, blind spots, fragile collections, critical points and dangerous equipment
improves: safe-RL benchmarks use simplified dynamics and VLA benchmarks measure success without built-in safety constraints
setup: AI2-THOR with ProcTHOR scenes and Objaverse assets; mobile robot with arm
scale: 3 task types (Safety-ObjNav, Safety-PickUp, Safety-Fetch); 150K procedurally generated scenes; 5 safety-critical component types
real_validation: The aligned policy was deployed for Safety-PickUp on a platform with dual Realman RM75-6F arms; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
vla_results: SPOC variants, EmbCLIP, Embodied-Codebook, FLaRe, PoliFormer and the proposed ISA; ISA cuts safety cost by 83.58% while keeping task performance
status: Introduced inside the SafeVLA method paper; project page with data and models
note: Venue from the arXiv comment (spotlight). Navigation-heavy mobile manipulation; baselines are SPOC-style policies, not tabletop VLAs.

name: HazardArena
evaluates: semantic safety: whether a policy withholds an action that is motorically identical to a safe one but unsafe in its visual-linguistic context
improves: evaluation measures completion and not whether the action was permissible in context
setup: MuJoCo; built on the VLABench task framework; Franka Panda
scale: 51 risk scenarios with safe and unsafe twins (10-task main suite); 7 hazard categories; 1,000 safe demonstrations
real_validation: Five task families were run on a Franka Panda with 100 trials per condition using mitigated props: safe-only fine-tuning gave 46.0% safe and 39.6% unsafe success; refusal-augmented training cut unsafe success to 0.4%.
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT, VLA-Adapter, NORA, pi0; safe-only fine-tuning raises unsafe-twin execution together with safe success (pi0: 0.47 safe, 0.44 unsafe)
status: No code or project URL found; listed as submitted
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: ForesightSafety-VLA
evaluates: process-level safety across physical interaction (force, thermal, spatial boundary, collaboration, sequencing), instruction-side and perception-side hazards
improves: safety is absent from VLA benchmarks, reduced to sparse collision checks, or mixed with generic task failure

scale: 66 safety-augmented scenarios; 13 categories in three families; structure levels L0-L2, language W0-W4, vision V0-V4
vla_results: OpenVLA-OFT, RDT, Diffusion Policy, ACT with full metrics (safe success 0.42, 0.30, 0.24, 0.20); pi0.5, pi0, DexVLA and others in partial runs; no baseline is fully safe

name: SafeManip
evaluates: temporal safety properties monitored on low-level rollouts: collision and contact, grasp and release stability, cross-contamination, action onset, mechanism, containment, enclosure
improves: benchmarks cover either physical consequences or the semantic structure of safe behaviour, not temporal specifications on executed motion
setup: RoboCasa365 and LIBERO
scale: 90 tasks (50 RoboCasa365, 40 LIBERO); 8 property categories; 50 rollouts per task
vla_results: pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.5 and N1.6, RLDX-1, Cosmos Policy, OpenVLA; on RoboCasa365 more capable policies violate more (r = +0.66), on LIBERO the reverse (r = -0.99)

name: SafeStage
evaluates: unsafe success across the task lifecycle: hazards present in the initial state, during execution, and left in the final state
improves: benchmarks do not check relation-dependent preconditions, execution-time interactions or post-completion physical states
setup: Isaac Sim (PhysX); simulated DROID setup with Franka Panda and Robotiq gripper
scale: 97 scenarios (27 initial-state, 40 execution-time, 30 final-state); 3 prompt conditions
vla_results: pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, DreamZero, Cosmos3 Nano Policy without fine-tuning; aggregate success 33.74% but safe success 9.84%; about 71% of successful rollouts are unsafe
status: Code repository listed

name: OopsieVerse
evaluates: damage caused during household manipulation: mechanical (impact, compression, tension), thermal and fluid damage measured by a simulator plugin
improves: simulators do not detect or quantify the damage that unsafe interactions would cause
setup: DamageSim plugin on OmniGibson (BEHAVIOR-1K) and MuJoCo (RoboCasa); Franka Panda for real tests
scale: 32 tasks (21 unique designs across two simulators); 450 demonstrations for learning experiments
real_validation: Shelving and pouring were run on a Franka Panda: damage-aware policies reached 65% safe completion vs 5% for the baseline; method transfer, damage agreement described qualitatively.
vla_results: GR00T: 8-92% completion but 0-8% safe completion on OmniGibson tasks; pi0: 17.5% completion and 0% safe completion on RoboCasa tasks; imitation and RL baselines with health feedback also tested
status: Project site with code
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session.

name: ManiGuard-Bench
evaluates: specification-grounded safety: LTLf spatial invariants and temporal ordering constraints monitored during contact-rich tabletop tasks, in- and out-of-distribution
improves: manipulation benchmarks do not define or monitor safety during execution, and formal-specification benchmarks lack contact-rich trajectories and safety-annotated data
setup: Isaac Sim / OmniGibson (PhysX); BDDL predicates; Franka Panda
scale: 200 base tasks expanded to 1,000 scenarios (1 in-distribution and 4 shifted conditions each); 6 task families; 8,000 demonstrations
real_validation: Three fine-tuned policies were run on a physical Franka on two task families (30 rollouts per cell); sim-real correlation is reported: r = 0.91 for success, 0.88 for safe success, 0.09 for violation rate.
vla_results: pi0.5, pi0, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.6; zero-shot safe success 0.0-1.8%, fine-tuned 7.5-29.8%; a large share of successful rollouts violate a specification
status: Project page, code and Hugging Face collection listed
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. The only entry in this slice with a numeric sim-real correlation.

name: BeSafe-Bench (BSB-EmbodiedVLA)
evaluates: operational safety of a VLA during LIBERO manipulation, reported as success, safety and success-and-safe rates
improves: agent-safety benchmarks rarely execute actions in functional environments, and embodied evaluation ignores behavioural safety
setup: LIBERO-90 tasks extended through VLA-Arena; 7-DoF arm
scale: One of four tracks in a 1,312-task agent-safety benchmark; the size of the VLA track was not extracted
vla_results: OpenVLA 49.81% success and 30% success-and-safe; OpenVLA-OFT 56.85% and 35.19%; pi0.5 23.89% and 13.89%
status: No code or project URL found
note: Details taken from an automated extraction of the arXiv HTML opened in this session. Mainly a web, mobile and LLM-agent benchmark; the VLA track is a small part. The arXiv ID is 2603.25747 while the API lists a first-version date of 2026-01-30.

name: SoftVTBench
evaluates: safe handling of deformable objects: a rollout counts as safe only without drops and with peak deformation below a calibrated threshold
improves: success-only evaluation overstates performance because many goal-completing rollouts violate physical safety limits
setup: Isaac Sim 4.5.0 with PhysX 5 FEM soft bodies; Franka Panda with GelSight Mini tactile sensors
scale: 40 tasks in 4 matched suites; 2,000 demonstration episodes; 33 assets (19 rigid, 14 deformable)
vla_results: pi0.5 vision-only: 70.4% goal success and 21.4% safety success on the soft-object suite; pi0.5 visuo-tactile: 71.8% and 35.6%
status: Project page available; described as an early version
